newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian death crash probe lists army failings.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian death crash probe lists army failings.

text.p: An inquiry into Australia's worst military disaster in three decades, a helicopter crash which killed 18 soldiers last June, said on Thursday a string of defence force failings caused the tragedy.

Defence Minister Ian McLachlan told parliament a special board of inquiry had blamed the crash of two army Black Hawk helicopters during a night anti-terrorist exercise on "a chain of events" that included inexperience and bad planning.
"There was a chain of events that successively and cumulatively led to a situation where the accident became what the board describes as the inevitable outcome," he said.
"The board found a number of long-term systemic factors which contributed to the accident."

McLachlan said these included a high rate of unservicability among the army's Black Hawks in the two years before the accident and the loss of a large number of experienced pilots, eroding the army's "bank of experience and skill".
"These factors clearly affected the experience levels amongst Black Hawk crews and prevented them from gaining sufficient flying experience for the special counter-terrorism operations," he said.
The probe also uncovered failings in the planning preparation, rehearsal and conduct of the exercise.
The inquiry found no mechanical defects and no fault with the Black Hawk design.
"In fact, the aircraft design unquestionably prevented a greater death toll," McLachlan said.

Military authorities reviewed the board's findings before they were publicly released and are considering disciplinary action against three service personnel and administrative action against two more over the accident, McLachlan said.
Further details were being kept secret until a final decision was made.
"Nothing that we can do will fully compensate for the loss of those 18 Australian servicemen," McLachlan said.
"All of us have been profoundly affected by this tragedy, but I hope that some consolation can be found in the knowledge that those who perished did so in the service of their country.

The inquiry said the crash occurred after one helicopter turned in front of the second during the night exercise in far north Queensland state, aimed at practicing a mission to free hostages held by terrorists.
But the probe said there was no single cause of the tragedy.

Acting on the board's almost 80 recommendations, McLachlan said the government would establish a special military air safety agency, review training and command procedures, and look at new and better equipment, including mid-air crash alarms and crash data recorders.
The army will also look at a series of measures, including bonuses, to keep pilots in the service longer.
Fifteen members of the elite Special Air Service commandos and three army airmen died in the crash, the worst peacetime military disaster since two navy warships collided in 1964, killing 82 sailors.
Australia's fleet of Black Hawks has been plagued by structural fatigue problems. In 1995, only five of the 38 Black Hawks were available for service.
